request.brief: Receive the Haldane Mission (Imperial Germany, 1912). Opens talks with Britain over naval construction, and grants 10 naval XP. Build one large central emblem: an unsigned ivory diplomatic folio, with the unmistakable compact side profile of a 1912 dreadnought embossed in dark steel across it. Use one shallow, aged brass rectangular frame over a complete deep blue enamel backplate. Broad readable edges, simple interior, subtle off-white highlight and charcoal steel, no tiny overlays. Frame sits wholly inside the canvas. Entire interior opaque and complete; real transparency only beyond the silhouette. Aim for 100×88 directly at generation; no lettering, no numerals, no portraits, no flags, no map, no modern ship shapes. Separate logical visual planes: backplate, frame, then centered central motif; each has crisp edges. Match the two vanilla HOI4 assets in age, relief, palette and painterly material. Use them as style references only.

prompt.text:
Create one Hearts of Iron IV national focus icon: Receive the Haldane Mission (Imperial Germany, 1912). Opens talks with Britain over naval construction, and grants 10 naval XP. Build one large central emblem: an unsigned ivory diplomatic folio, with the unmistakable compact side profile of a 1912 dreadnought embossed in dark steel across it. Use one shallow, aged brass rectangular frame over a complete deep blue enamel backplate. Broad readable edges, simple interior, subtle off-white highlight and charcoal steel, no tiny overlays. Frame sits wholly inside the canvas. Entire interior opaque and complete; real transparency only beyond the silhouette. Aim for 100×88 directly at generation; no lettering, no numerals, no portraits, no flags, no map, no modern ship shapes. Separate logical visual planes: backplate, frame, then centered central motif; each has crisp edges. Match the two vanilla HOI4 assets in age, relief, palette and painterly material. Use them as style references only.

Requirements:
- Take the frame, outline and overall form from the style anchor images, not from a fixed family form; the size, transparency, margin and readability requirements here still apply.
- Flags and ribbons use invented colours, never a real country's flag, unless the brief names that country.
- The subject is large: it fills most of the emblem and may overlap its frame, never a small figure inside a wide empty plaque.
- A strong central symbol that supports the focus's story, readable contrast at 100x88 pixels.
- Real transparent background around the emblem: no backdrop behind it.
- Leave a small empty margin around the emblem.

Reference images, in the order attached:
1. style anchor: match its painting style, palette and level of detail
2. style anchor: match its painting style, palette and level of detail
The style anchor images were chosen for this image. Match their form, framing, materials and palette; the vanilla form described under Requirements applies only where they do not show one.

Avoid: text; letters or numbers; watermark or signature; a drawn checkerboard pattern; a square backdrop behind the subject.

Produce exactly one image.
negative: a square backdrop behind the subject

style_sources.method: descriptors (Lab mean/std, saturation, Sobel edge density, alpha coverage, dark-outline share, 6-bin hue histogram) are standardised; deterministic k-medoids (PAM, no random start, candidates ordered by content hash) picks up to 24 images for statistics and drift. Up to 4 images are sent: a pinned style as ordered; otherwise nation-specific files are left out unless the brief names the country, about half the slots are drawn from the files whose names best match the brief's words and themes and the rest from the family's most style-typical generic files, all seeded by a hash of the family, asset and brief
